cleared.check: Symbol comparison of the Nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 release binaries of commit b72783f (amd64 sha256 a142fcbe..., arm64 ba1fec28..., equal to cycle 23's nitro-binaries.sha256, taken again from Docker Hub layers 35a7cb1a and f4d1a9c1 of offchainlabs/nitro-node) against go-ethereum v1.17.10 core/vm (proxy.golang.org module zip, sha256 6e7ac323...), the *_arbitrum.go files of OffchainLabs/go-ethereum master, and holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 (proxy.golang.org zip, sha256 b3998d66...). pclntab lists 540 core/vm and 129 uint256 functions in each binary, with the same names in both.
cleared.result: uint256: the binary has no function that v1.3.2 lacks; the 27 source-only names are small helpers the compiler inlined (lsh64, rsh128, umulHop, umulStep, reciprocal2by1, udivrem2by1, subMulTo, addTo and others) or constructors the node never calls. core/vm: the binary-only names are (*Contract).Jumpdest (an accessor that returns the jumpDests interface at Contract+0x30), (*EVM).ChainRules (returns a pointer to evm+0x100), (*p256Verify).SetArbosVersion (stores one word), DefaultTxProcessor.IsCalldataPricingIncrease7976And7981Enabled, newArbitrumAmsterdamInstructionSet, and the closures of makeDup and makePush, which v1.17.10 replaced by opDup1..16 and opPush3..32. v1.17.10 also has execUntraced and execTraced (the generated interpreter) and layeredJumpDests, which the binary does not contain; the binary's (*EVM).Run (5,568 bytes) dispatches every handler by an indirect call through the operation table and contains no adc, sbb or div instruction. Package variables cannot be listed from the binaries, which carry no symbol table or DWARF; the data addresses that the arithmetic and jump handlers read are listed in the next entry. None of these names touches arithmetic, shifts, comparisons or jump analysis.

cleared.check: Every call target and every data reference of opMulmod, opAddmod, opMul, opDiv, opSdiv, opMod, opSmod, opExp, opSHL, opSHR, opSAR, opByte, opSignExtend, opLt, opGt, opSlt, opSgt, opEq, opIszero, opAdd, opSub, opJump, opJumpi, validJumpdest, isCode, codeBitmapInternal, mapJumpDests.Load/Store and the uint256 functions they reach, in both binaries (objdump and llvm-objdump 18 text, resolved against pclntab).
cleared.result: Each arithmetic handler calls exactly one uint256 method (MulMod, AddMod, Mul, Div, SDiv, Mod, SMod, Exp, Lsh, Rsh, SRsh, Byte, ExtendSign, Slt, Sgt) plus runtime.morestack_noctxt and runtime.panicBounds; opLt, opGt, opEq, opIszero, opAdd and opSub are inline. MulMod reaches umul, Reciprocal, reduce4, udivrem and Mod; AddMod reaches Mod and udivrem; Div, Mod and SMod reach udivrem, udivremBy1 and udivremKnuth (on arm64 also math/bits.Div64); Exp reaches Mul and squared; SRsh reaches Rsh. The only data they read are a 32 byte zero constant (AddMod, amd64 0x3f093e8), the constant one (Exp, amd64 0x3f06d20) and the runtime error value passed to gopanic in Reciprocal. opJump and opJumpi read the abort flag at evm+0x170 and two error values. No handler or helper reads or writes a map, a sync.Pool, a table indexed by operands or any other writable global, so commit b72783f keeps no memo or cache in front of the arithmetic. The only cache on the jump path is the jumpDests map keyed by code hash (isCode, map Load/Store), which an earlier cycle tested on chain (OPCODES.md, Arbitrum family row: one address given code with and without a JUMPDEST at the same offset jumps, fails and jumps again). Each handler entry appears once as a funcval in read-only data (amd64 opMulmod at 0x6ba9028, arm64 at 0x6346d78), so the jump table calls the handler itself with no wrapper. A PrecompileCache type exists (precompile_cache.go of the fork, also in v1.17.10); the PoolManager calls no precompile.

The not-reached instructions are the stack growth and panic paths. MulModWithReciprocal is in the binaries but no handler calls it. The first amd64 pass stopped on 691 SIGNEXTEND cases at movsx rbx,bl in ExtendSign (0xc61dbe), an instruction the x86-64 model lacked; movsx and bts were added to the model (scripts/models.py) and all amd64 sets were run again from the start. No function had to be skipped for a call into the Go runtime: memmove is modelled in Python, and morestack and the panic entries stop the model and were never reached.

leadResults.answer: Answered from the release binaries of commit b72783f without the source. The core/vm and uint256 functions in pclntab match go-ethereum v1.17.10 and uint256 v1.3.2 by name except for Arbitrum accessors and the older makeDup and makePush closures. The arithmetic, shift, comparison and jump handlers call only stock uint256 methods and read no writable global, so there is no memo or cache in front of them. Run in x86-64 and AArch64 models, they gave the reference word on 2,866,788 and 2,866,788 cases with no mismatch; jump analysis matched on every program, planted faults were caught, and 2,000 vectors sent twice to Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain matched.
